title: Singular negative olla
summary: Form en ole, et ole, and ei ole with singular subjects.
objectives: Choose en, et, or ei from the subject.
Place ole after the negative verb.

sections.title: Finnish has a negative verb
paragraphs: Finnish negation uses a small verb that changes with the subject. For singular persons, use en, et, and ei.
The main verb olla then appears as ole: minä en ole, sinä et ole, hän ei ole.

sections.title: Two verb words, one negative meaning
paragraphs: The negative verb carries person agreement. Ole follows it and does not change across these three forms.
Keep both words. A single English word such as “isn’t” still corresponds to two Finnish verb words.

examples.english: He or she is not tired.
steps: Olla becomes ole after the negative verb.

commonMistakes: Do not use ei for every person.
Do not keep the affirmative form after en, et, or ei.
